title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
summary: Kaspersky GReAT experts discovered a new UEFI bootkit, BlackX. It exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) and is similar to the BlackLotus bootkit.

title: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
summary: We discuss the incident involving the leak of information about vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Kaspersky solutions detect the PHP2Shell exploit: we’ll walk you through examples using KEDR, KATA, and KES.

title: Operation FlashHole: Lazarus breaks security, defies control
summary: Kaspersky researchers analyze Operation FlashHole – a recent complex attack by Lazarus, involving a sophisticated malware set, watering-hole technique and abuse of CrossWeb EX financial security software.

title: The journey of a paper unicorn: adventures inside a modern warehouse
summary: Kaspersky experts explain the security issues affecting warehouse environments. We break down initial access vectors specific to warehouses, and discuss the impact of a compromise.

title: MacSync under the microscope: new delivery methods and a new payload
summary: We look at a new version of the MacSync macOS stealer with a backdoor module that targets crypto enthusiasts and developers.

title: Group Policy hijacked: PAYLOAD ransomware weaponizes Active Directory GPO
summary: Kaspersky GERT experts dive into the technical incident analysis of PAYLOAD ransomware: an encryptionless, binary-less operation that abused Active Directory mechanisms for managing Group Policy Objects.

title: The Odyssey and Trojans again: MovieReaper attacks users in multiple countries through compromised torrents
summary: Kaspersky experts have discovered a new MovieReaper campaign. The multi-stage Trojan spreads through movie torrents, such as The Odyssey, and uses the Solana blockchain to hide its C2 infrastructure.

title: NightEagle targets Russian companies
summary: Kaspersky GERT experts have uncovered a new campaign by the NightEagle APT, featuring the GhostContainer backdoor and tools hosted on GitHub. The group is also exploiting vulnerabilities in Active Directory and RDP.

title: Angry Birds: Toy Ghouls’ new toys
summary: Kaspersky GERT experts have discovered new backdoors used by the Toy Ghouls group. One version of the backdoor uses the HiveMQ MQTT broker as its command-and-control server; the other uses the Matrix-based Element messenger.

title: Mirage Kitten targeting aviation and FinTech sectors across the Middle East and Africa with a new malware set
summary: Kaspersky researchers have discovered new Mirage Kitten attacks using previously undocumented malware families: NodeRabbit in Node.js and PollCat in JavaScript.
